questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

What is the inverse of f(x) = x - 4

feedback.text: This repeats the original function instead of reversing it.
Multiplication by 4 does not undo subtracting 4.
Division by 4 would undo multiplication by 4, not subtraction.
Correct. Adding 4 undoes subtracting 4.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

What is the inverse of f(x) = 3x²

feedback.text: This repeats the original function.
Correct. Dividing by 3 undoes multiplying by 3.
Subtraction does not undo multiplication by 3.
Addition does not undo multiplication by 3.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

If f(8) = -2 and f has an inverse, what is f(-2)

feedback.text: Correct. The inverse maps the output -2 back to the input 8.
This multiplies the values and does not represent the inverse.
This keeps the output instead of reversing the relationship.
This subtracts values but does not use inverse meaning.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

What graph relationship do inverse functions have

answer.text: They are reflected across the x-axis.

feedback.text: Reflection across the x-axis changes output signs, not inverse relationships.

answer.text: They are reflected across the y-axis.

feedback.text: Reflection across the y-axis changes input signs, not inverse relationships.

answer.text: They are reflected across the line y = x.

feedback.text: Correct. Inverses swap x and y coordinates.

answer.text: They are vertical shifts of each other.

feedback.text: Inverse functions are not identified by a vertical shift.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

What is the inverse of f(x) = x / 5

feedback.text: Correct. Multiplying by 5 undoes dividing by 5.
This repeats the original function.
Addition does not undo division by 5.
Subtraction does not undo division by 5.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q06

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

What is the inverse of f(x) = 2x + 1

feedback.text: Correct. Subtract 1, then divide by 2.
This uses the wrong operation to undo +1.
This leaves the +1 instead of undoing it.
This does not undo the multiplication by 2.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q07

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.12

Which restriction makes f(x) = x² one-to-one

feedback.text: This describes output values, not a domain restriction.
Over all real numbers, negative and positive inputs can share the same output.
Removing only 0 does not prevent pairs such as -2 and 2 from sharing an output.
Correct. Restricting to nonnegative inputs makes x² pass the horizontal line test.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q08

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

If f(6) = 11, what must be true about f

feedback.text: Correct. The inverse statement means f maps 11 to 6.
This reverses the inverse relationship incorrectly.
The output should be 6, not 11.
There is no sign change implied by inverse notation.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q09

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

What is f(f(x)) for inverse functions f and f

feedback.text: That would describe additive opposites, not inverse functions.
That would describe reciprocal products, not function inverses.
The inverse should undo f, leaving x.
Correct. A function composed with its inverse returns the original input.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q10

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

What is the inverse of f(x) = x + 12

feedback.text: Multiplication does not undo addition.
Correct. Subtracting 12 undoes adding 12.
Division does not undo addition.
This repeats the original function.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q11

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.12

Which test helps determine whether a graph has an inverse function without restricting the domain

feedback.text: Distance formula does not determine invertibility.
The vertical line test checks whether a relation is a function, not whether it is one-to-one.
Correct. Passing the horizontal line test shows the function is one-to-one.
This is not a standard test for invertibility.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q12

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.13

A function converts Celsius to Fahrenheit. What does the inverse convert

feedback.text: Correct. The inverse reverses Celsius-to-Fahrenheit conversion.
The inverse reverses the original conversion.
The inverse does not keep the same input and output unit.
This is a different temperature conversion.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q13

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

Which ordered pair must appear on f if (2, 9) is on f

feedback.text: This changes the sign instead of switching coordinates.
Correct. Inverses switch input and output coordinates.
This changes the sign of the input.
This repeats the original ordered pair rather than reversing it.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q14

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

What is the inverse of f(x) = (x - 3) / 4

feedback.text: This does not reverse both operations.
Correct. Multiply by 4, then add 3.
This repeats the same operation order.
This does not undo the subtraction correctly after multiplying.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q15

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.12

Why is f(x) = |x| not one-to-one on all real numbers

feedback.text: The graph decreases then increases, so this description is inaccurate.
It has a y-intercept at 0.
Its domain is all real numbers.

answer.text: Opposite inputs can produce the same output.

feedback.text: Correct. For example, f(-3) and f(3) both equal 3.

Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q16

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

Which equation shows correct inverse verification for f(x) = x + 2 and g(x) = x - 2

feedback.text: Adding does not verify inverse relationships.
Correct. f(g(x)) = (x - 2) + 2 = x.
Subtraction does not show the functions undo each other.
Multiplication is not inverse verification.

Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q17

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.13

If a function maps hours worked to pay earned, what does the inverse map

feedback.text: This does not reverse the relationship.
Correct. The inverse reverses the original input-output relationship.
This keeps the output unit unchanged.
This does not represent the inverse context.

Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q18

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

What is the inverse of f(x) = 5x - 10

feedback.text: This repeats the subtraction instead of undoing it.
This does not reverse the order of operations.
Correct. Add 10, then divide by 5.
This does not undo multiplication by 5.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q19

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.12

Which domain restriction can make f(x) = (x - 1) invertible

feedback.text: This is a range statement, not a domain restriction.
The full parabola is not one-to-one.
Removing the vertex does not remove all repeated outputs.
Correct. One side of the parabola is one-to-one.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q20

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

If f and g are inverses, what is g(f(4))

feedback.text: Inverse composition returns the original input, not zero.
This confuses inverse functions with reciprocal products.
Correct. g(f(4)) returns the original input 4.
The outer inverse should undo f.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q21

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

Which first step best supports a solution for Inverse Functions and Domain Restrictions

answer.text: Skip directly to an answer without naming the given information.

feedback.text: Skipping the setup often leads to using the wrong method.

answer.text: Identify the given representation, quantities, and restrictions before calculating.

feedback.text: Correct. A strong Precalculus solution begins by identifying the representation and restrictions so the method matches the task.

answer.text: Use any formula from a different unit.

feedback.text: A different unit may use different assumptions or tools.

answer.text: Base the answer only on how a graph or expression appears.

feedback.text: Appearance can be misleading unless it is supported by values or relationships.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q22

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

What evidence should a student use when explaining Inverse Functions and Domain Restrictions

answer.text: Use labeled values, equations, graphs, or tables from the problem as evidence.

feedback.text: Correct. Evidence must come from the given mathematical representation, not from a guess or unrelated rule.

answer.text: Ignore labels and units because they are not part of the calculation.

feedback.text: Labels and units help determine what the quantities mean.

answer.text: Use a future topic even when the current lesson gives enough information.

feedback.text: The current lesson evidence should be used before reaching for later topics.

answer.text: Use the longest answer choice as evidence.

feedback.text: Answer length is not mathematical evidence.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q23

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

Which response best shows mastery of Inverse Functions and Domain Restrictions

answer.text: Change the given values to make the computation easier.

feedback.text: Changing given values changes the problem.

answer.text: Give only a final number with no reasoning.

feedback.text: A final number alone does not show how the relationship was used.

answer.text: Copy vocabulary without applying it to the problem.

feedback.text: Vocabulary must be connected to the actual representation or calculation.

answer.text: Show the steps, connect them to the lesson relationship, and interpret the result.

feedback.text: Correct. Mastery requires both accurate work and an interpretation connected to the lesson relationship.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q24

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

What should be checked before finalizing work involving Inverse Functions and Domain Restrictions

answer.text: Check only that the answer choice is short.

feedback.text: Length does not show correctness.

answer.text: Remove restrictions because they make the problem harder.

feedback.text: Restrictions are part of the mathematical meaning.

answer.text: Assume every representation has the same domain.

feedback.text: Different representations may show different restrictions.

answer.text: Check that notation, units, domain restrictions, and the final interpretation match the task.

feedback.text: Correct. These checks help confirm that the answer is mathematically valid for the stated task.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: PC_U01_L05_Q25

MLA Standard: MLA.PC.FA.11

Which error should be avoided when working with Inverse Functions and Domain Restrictions

feedback.text: Writing givens first is a helpful setup, not the error.

answer.text: Explaining why a theorem, identity, or model applies.

feedback.text: Explaining why a method applies strengthens the solution.

answer.text: Using an unrelated formula or visual pattern without checking the lesson conditions.

feedback.text: Correct. Appearance alone is not reliable; the method must match the conditions in the lesson.

answer.text: Checking the final answer in the context of the problem.

feedback.text: Checking in context is a good habit, not an error.\
